prompt:
Produce exactly one concise caption (one sentence) stating only visually verifiable facts. The caption must contain 2–6 discrete facts chosen strictly in this priority order when present: 
1) Legible text — if any text is clearly readable, transcribe it verbatim in quotes as the first fact; if text is not clearly legible, do not mention any text. 
2) Exact counts and canonical object types using numerals (e.g., "2 people", "1 bicycle"). 
3) Color/material/texture/localized markings with placement modifiers (e.g., "tan patch on mid-back", "bench with peeling green paint and rust spots"). 
4) Precise pose/action/orientation using short phrases (e.g., "mid-air, arms outstretched", "head lowered, tongue visible", "bending over sorting bags", "seen from behind"). 
5) Simple spatial layout using foreground/midground/background or left/right/center. 
6) Lighting/viewpoint/occlusion only if clearly visible (e.g., "bright sunlight casting sharp shadows", "strong reflection on wet sand", "elevated vantage; tree partially obscures façade"). 

Use numerals for counts, canonical nouns (person, dog, bench, sign, vehicle, goat, satellite dish, etc.), enclose any transcribed text in quotes, and separate facts compactly with commas or semicolons. Do not infer roles, age, emotions, intentions, or any non-visible context; do not guess unreadable text; avoid metaphors, slogans, or marketing language. Produce exactly one sentence, no lists, tags, JSON, multiple candidates, or extra commentary. Before emitting, ensure each stated fact is directly visible; omit anything you cannot visually confirm.
